sections.overview: This geometrid moth occurs across much of Europe and eastward into Siberia.
sections.identification: The adult has a wingspan of about 30–34 mm and usually rather indistinct wing markings.
sections.habitat: It occurs in woodland, clearings and wetlands where its larval food plants grow.
sections.diet: The larvae feed on trees including willow, poplar, birch and honeysuckle.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in spring, usually from April into May in Britain.
sections.reproduction: The larvae develop in late spring and early summer, and the pupa overwinters.
sections.ecology: For comparison, the related T. polycommata is recorded on privet and ash; see that profile.
sections.conservation: The British account describes it as fairly common across most of the islands; it gives no global assessment.
